properties.name: A CI run leaves a machine-readable record of which gates ran
properties.statement:
Every CI run leaves behind a machine-readable record of the gates it ran — gate name, exit code, duration, commit sha and timestamp — published as a build artifact. It is emitted by the runner that already reads the gate list from the workflow, so the record cannot drift from the set actually executed, and a run that executed nothing must be readable AS nothing rather than as an absence of failures.

SCOPE, STATED SO THE BOUNDARY IS NOT LOST: nothing writes this into the design automatically. Turning a run record into a Verification's status stays a deliberate act by a person or a session. The stronger form — CI setting status, last_run_at and commit on Verification nodes directly — is NOT required here, because it would make reflow2 the writer of a claim it elsewhere only records, and that question is still open.

WHAT IT IS FOR: 46 of this design's 312 checks have never run, 282 carry no executable form, and the rollups cannot tell an unrun check from a passing one. A dated run record with a commit behind it is also the missing source for quantities the closure reading currently counts at zero of fourteen.
